subject: general
question: What type of rocks mainly compose the Peninsular Plateau of India?

options.text: Recent volcanic lava deposits from plate margins
Layers of limestone and sandstone from marine origin
Old crystalline, igneous and metamorphic rocks
Young sedimentary rocks formed in coastal plains

solution:
The correct answer is __**Old crystalline, igneous and metamorphic rocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Peninsular Plateau of India is primarily composed of **old crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks** that are among the oldest geological formations in the world.
 
• It is a part of the Gondwana landmass and represents one of the most stable landforms, with its rocks dating back to the Precambrian era (about 4 billion years ago).
 
• This plateau includes **granites, gneisses, schists, and quartzites**, which are resistant to erosion, making it geologically stable.
 
• The region is rich in mineral resources such as **iron ore, manganese, gold, copper, and bauxite**, which have contributed significantly to India's industrial development.
 
• The Deccan Plateau, a major sub-region of the Peninsular Plateau, is characterized by vast expanses of basalt due to ancient volcanic activity, but the underlying structure remains dominated by crystalline rocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geological significance of the Peninsular Plateau:**

 
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is divided into two major regions: the **Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.**
 
• It is bounded by the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in the north and the Western and Eastern Ghats in the west and east, respectively.
 
• This region plays a vital role in shaping India's geography, climate, and economy due to its elevation, stability, and mineral wealth.
